title: regional-holdover-latch-and-kv-peacemaker-hotfix
author: Maya Chen
description: Background and motivation: We observed a class of incidents where short-lived regional egress flaps caused premature circuit reopen and aggressive KV eviction during failover, resulting in a cascade of cold-start latency for critical tenant traffic. This PR introduces two coordinated fixes: 1) a region-aware 'holdover latch' that extends the circuit 'soft-closed' window for a small, adaptive duration when downstream health signals are noisy, and 2) a 'KV peacemaker' mechanism that moves KV cache ownership into a transient soft-preserve state during regional handoffs so we avoid immediate wholesale eviction. Goals: reduce repeated cold-path penalties after transient network disruptions, stabilize SLOs for p95 latency during regional failover, and avoid noisy circuit flips. Summary of changes: - runtime/evac/holdover.go: new holdover latch implementation with adaptive backoff driven by recent heartbeat and probe deltas - runtime/evac/holdover_test.go: unit + property tests for latch edge cases - runtime/kv/peacemaker.go: soft-preserve state for shards during failover transitions with metrics hooks - runtime/kv/peacemaker_integration_test.go: integration tests simulating regional failover and gradual handoff - controlplane/config/flags.go: feature flag + rollout params (default: enabled for staged rollout) - telemetry/metrics/holdover_metrics.yaml: new metrics and dashboards references - docs/ops/regional-failover-playbook.md: updated playbook with explanation and rollback steps Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for holdover latch - [x] Integration test for KV handoff path - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated (new metric names documented) - [x] Feature flag gated and defaulted to staged rollout - [x] Post-deploy canary for 48 hours in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag; start with small canary in us-west-2 (10% of regional traffic), monitor p95/p99 and kv_cache_hit_ratio, then expand to other regions after 48h. If SLO regressions are detected, flip flag off or revert. Why this is different from earlier mitigations: previous approaches allowed immediate circuit re-open when health probes recovered briefly, which produced oscillation when egress paths were still unstable. The holdover latch uses time-weighted probe deltas and tenant-weighted penalties to avoid premature reopen for tenants with high cold-start cost. The KV peacemaker avoids aggressive eviction for a small window during the handoff, allowing warm-up to continue on surviving nodes. Production notes: low-risk code paths and guarded by feature flag. Expected telemetry: small increase in memory retention for short windows (tracked by kv_soft_preserve_memory_bytes) but large drop in cold-start p95 for targeted tenants. Refs: Linear ENG-2940, incident SUP-4123, earlier WIP PRs on regional failover.

release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize regional failover by introducing an adaptive holdover latch to reduce circuit oscillation and a KV peacemaker to avoid immediate cache eviction during handoffs. Enabled behind feature flag for staged rollout. Expected outcome: lower cold-start p95 during transient egress flaps; may temporarily increase soft-preserve memory usage (tracked).
operator_instructions: Post-merge: enable feature flag for canary region (us-west-2) at 10% traffic. Monitor p95 latency (route/model), kv_soft_preserve_memory_bytes, holdover_count_by_region. If p95 increases or memory pressure spikes, disable flag. Full rollout after 48h of stability.
incident_correlation: This PR addresses SUP-4123 incident series where repeated egress blips caused oscillation and cold-cache penalties; we correlate a 60% reduction in cold-path p95 in canary runs.
notes_on_risk: Low — feature-flagged and conservative defaults. Risk surface: modest memory retention and potential longer soft-fail windows for some tenants; mitigations included per-shard caps and memory-pressure throttle.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover timestamp skew, latch hysteresis, and tenant-weighted penalties. Integration simulates egress flap and validates KV warm-path retention across handoff. Load tests show no regression in steady-state throughput.
post_deploy_checks:
- verify holdover_count_by_region remains < 1% of requests during steady state
- kv_cache_hit_ratio recovers within 30s for canary tenants after handoff
- no new OOMs or eviction storms in cluster metrics
